subject: humanities
notes: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are a group of more than 700 natural shelters in sandstone hills in central India.
Many of the shelters contain paintings, mostly in red and white, showing animals, hunting scenes, and dancing.
The oldest paintings are thought to be at least 10,000 years old, while others were made in much later periods.
Archaeologist V. S. Wakankar brought the shelters to scholars' attention in 1957.
In 2003, UNESCO named Bhimbetka a World Heritage Site.
stem: The student wants to introduce the Bhimbetka rock shelters to an unfamiliar audience and emphasize the long span of time over which their paintings were made. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The oldest of the paintings in the Bhimbetka rock shelters are thought to have been made at least 10,000 years ago.
choices.B: Bhimbetka, a group of more than 700 rock shelters in the sandstone hills of central India, holds paintings, mostly in red and white, of animals, hunting scenes, and dancing.
choices.C: Brought to scholars' attention by V. S. Wakankar in 1957, the Bhimbetka rock shelters of central India became a World Heritage Site in 2003.
choices.D: Bhimbetka, a group of rock shelters in central India, holds paintings made over a vast span of time, from at least 10,000 years ago to much later periods.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: introduce the site (what and where it is) and stress how long a period the paintings cover. The span runs from at least 10,000 years ago to much later periods. Only one choice introduces the site and presents that full span.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It gives the age of the oldest paintings, but an age is not a span, and it does not introduce the site to a reader who has never heard of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It introduces the site and describes the paintings but says nothing about when they were made. This is the most attractive near miss because it is the fullest introduction.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It gives the site's modern history, not the period over which the paintings were made.
explanation.D: Correct. It identifies the site and stresses the span of time from the oldest paintings to much later ones.
